import re
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
SITE = ROOT / "website"
PAGES_URL = "https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/"

ALLOWED_EXTERNAL = {
    "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi",
    "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/issues",
    "https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat",
    "https://docs.astral.sh/uv/",
    "https://modelcontextprotocol.io",
    PAGES_URL,
}

MILESTONE_DATE = re.compile(
    r"\b(Q[1-4]|Jan(uary)?|Feb(ruary)?|Mar(ch)?|Apr(il)?|May|Jun(e)?|"
    r"Jul(y)?|Aug(ust)?|Sep(t(ember)?)?|Oct(ober)?|Nov(ember)?|Dec(ember)?)[ -]20\d\d\b"
)

EMOJI = re.compile("[\u2600-\u27bf\U0001f300-\U0001faff]")


class Doc(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.lang = None
        self.charset = False
        self.viewport = False
        self.title = ""
        self.ids: set[str] = set()
        self.hrefs: list[str] = []
        self.refs: list[str] = []
        self.headings: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
        self.tags: list[str] = []
        self.metas: dict[str, str] = {}
        self.theme_colors: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        self.text: list[str] = []
        self._in_title = False
        self._heading: tuple[int, list[str]] | None = None

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        a = dict(attrs)
        self.tags.append(tag)
        if tag == "html":
            self.lang = a.get("lang")
        elif tag == "title":
            self._in_title = True
        elif tag == "meta":
            if a.get("charset"):
                self.charset = True
            if a.get("name") == "viewport":
                self.viewport = True
            if a.get("name") == "theme-color":
                self.theme_colors.append((a.get("content", ""), a.get("media", "")))
            key = a.get("property") or a.get("name")
            if key:
                self.metas[key] = a.get("content", "")
        elif tag == "a" and a.get("href"):
            self.hrefs.append(a["href"])
        elif tag in ("link", "script", "img"):
            ref = a.get("href") or a.get("src")
            if ref:
                self.refs.append(ref)
        if a.get("id"):
            self.ids.add(a["id"])
        if re.fullmatch(r"h[1-6]", tag):
            self._heading = (int(tag[1]), [])

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag == "title":
            self._in_title = False
        elif self._heading and tag == f"h{self._heading[0]}":
            level, parts = self._heading
            self.headings.append((level, " ".join("".join(parts).split())))
            self._heading = None

    def handle_data(self, data):
        self.text.append(data)
        if self._in_title:
            self.title += data
        if self._heading:
            self._heading[1].append(data)


def parse(name: str) -> Doc:
    doc = Doc()
    doc.feed((SITE / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return doc


def test_lang_charset_viewport():
    doc = parse("index.html")
    assert doc.lang == "en"
    assert doc.charset
    assert doc.viewport


def test_title_and_description():
    doc = parse("index.html")
    assert "Agentic ODI" in doc.title
    assert len(doc.title.strip()) <= 60
    desc = doc.metas.get("description", "")
    assert 0 < len(desc) <= 160


def test_single_h1_and_ordered_headings():
    levels = [lv for lv, _ in parse("index.html").headings]
    assert levels.count(1) == 1
    assert levels[0] == 1
    for prev, cur in zip(levels, levels[1:], strict=False):
        assert cur <= prev + 1


def test_landmarks_and_section_ids():
    doc = parse("index.html")
    for landmark in ("header", "main", "footer"):
        assert landmark in doc.tags
    assert {"problem", "insight", "how", "run", "status"} <= doc.ids


def test_no_dead_internal_anchors():
    doc = parse("index.html")
    internal = [h[1:] for h in doc.hrefs if h.startswith("#")]
    assert internal, "expected in-page anchors"
    assert set(internal) <= doc.ids


def test_local_resources_exist_and_stylesheet_present():
    doc = parse("index.html")
    local = [r for r in doc.refs if not r.startswith(("http://", "https://"))]
    assert local
    for ref in local:
        assert (SITE / ref).is_file(), f"missing resource: {ref}"
    assert "assets/style.css" in local
    assert "assets/favicon.svg" in local
    assert "assets/favicon.png" in local


def test_no_third_party_resources():
    for ref in parse("index.html").refs:
        if ref.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
            assert ref in ALLOWED_EXTERNAL, f"off-allowlist resource: {ref}"
        else:
            assert ref.startswith("assets/"), f"unexpected resource: {ref}"


def test_external_links_https_and_allowlisted():
    for href in parse("index.html").hrefs:
        if href.startswith("#"):
            continue
        assert href.startswith("https://"), href
        assert href in ALLOWED_EXTERNAL, href


def test_social_cards_and_theme_colors():
    doc = parse("index.html")
    m = doc.metas
    assert m.get("og:type") == "website"
    assert m.get("og:site_name") == "Agentic ODI"

    assert len(doc.theme_colors) == 2
    assert any("prefers-color-scheme: light" in x for x in media)
    assert any("prefers-color-scheme: dark" in x for x in media)

    text = (SITE / "index.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    core = (ROOT / "packages" / "core" / "src" / "agentic_odi_core" / "models.py").read_text(
        encoding="utf-8"
    )

    doc = parse("404.html")
    assert doc.lang == "en"
    assert any(lv == 1 for lv, _ in doc.headings)
    assert PAGES_URL in doc.hrefs
    assert not doc.refs, "404.html must not depend on relative assets"

from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
SITE = ROOT / "website"
TOOLS = ROOT / "website" / "tools"


def _get_index_html():
    return (SITE / "index.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def test_script_idempotency():
    """Running the sync script twice produces identical output."""
    import subprocess

    result1 = subprocess.run(
        ["uv", "run", "python", "website/tools/sync-readme.py"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        cwd=ROOT,
    )
    assert result1.returncode == 0, f"First run failed: {result1.stderr}"

    html1 = _get_index_html()

    result2 = subprocess.run(
        ["uv", "run", "python", "website/tools/sync-readme.py"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        cwd=ROOT,
    )
    assert result2.returncode == 0, f"Second run failed: {result2.stderr}"

    html2 = _get_index_html()

    assert html1 == html2, "Sync script is not idempotent — output differs between runs"

### Install layout

```
~/.local/share/agentic-odi/
  ├── versions/<version>/
  │   └── odi (and bundled files)
  └── current -> versions/<version>

~/.local/bin/
  ├── odi -> ../share/agentic-odi/current/odi
  ├── odipm
  ├── odi-cli
  └── agentic-odi

~/.config/agentic-odi/  # state/preferences
```

Environment variables: `AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR` (override install root), `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_BIN_HOME`. The default backend is `local` (`--backend local`); no MCP server is required.

### Unsigned binaries

macOS may quarantine downloaded binaries: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ~/.local/bin/odi` (if needed). Windows SmartScreen may show a warning for unsigned binaries; choose "More info → Run anyway" if you trust the release.

### Release automation

Releases are cut and published by CI with no approval step:

1. Conventional commits land on `main`; `release-please` opens or updates the release PR.
2. The `release-please` workflow arms auto-merge on that PR. `main` requires the `CI green` check (ruleset `main-requires-ci-green`), so the PR merges itself as soon as CI passes — nobody clicks merge.
3. The merge cuts tag `vX.Y.Z` and the GitHub Release; the tag starts the `release` and `Tauri Release` workflows, which attach the CLI archives, `checksums.txt`, the install scripts, and the desktop bundles to it.
4. `e2e-install` runs after `release` succeeds and installs the published binary on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

**One-time setup (GitHub App).** GitHub holds workflow runs that start from `GITHUB_TOKEN`-authored pushes ("This workflow requires approval from a maintainer") and ignores the tag such a push creates, which is why releases used to need a maintainer. A release-only GitHub App avoids both:

1. Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App, with permissions: Contents `Read and write`, Issues `Read and write`, Pull requests `Read and write` (no webhook).
2. Install the App on this repository.
3. Add repository secrets `RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID` (the App's client ID) and `RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (a generated private key).

Until those secrets exist, the `release-please` workflow logs a warning and falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`: releases still happen, but the release PR needs a maintainer approval and merge, and the tag will not start the asset builds. After adding the secrets, re-run the workflow (`gh workflow run release-please.yml`) or push to `main` so the open release PR is re-driven by the App.

To check the installer without cutting a release, run `bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh` — it serves a simulated release over HTTP and exercises `scripts/install.sh` end to end (CI runs it too).

## ☁️ Deployment

The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**, Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents.

### 🧪 Test Chat (UI)

Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser:

> **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)**

### 🔌 MCP Server Endpoint

Integrate via the MCP protocol at:

> **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a client.

## 🗺️ Roadmap & Next Steps

As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include:

- [x] **External MCP client connector**: Pluggable connectors package with an HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests.
- [ ] **Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts**: Turn connector records into jobs, outcomes, or evidence without mixing connector plumbing into the ODI store.
- [ ] **Additional connector kinds**: REST/webhooks and similar integrations implementing the same `Connector` protocol.
- [ ] **ODI Schema Definition**: Define standardized Pydantic models for *Jobs*, *Steps*, and *Outcomes*.
- [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: Extend `cli/` so the ODI dataset can be created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current MCP path.
- [ ] **Context Tooling**: Replace the dummy `greet` tool with capabilities like `get_job_map(job_id)` or `evaluate_outcome(statement)`.
- [ ] **Data Persistence Layer**: Connect the fastmcp server to a lightweight vector or relational database containing actual user research data.
- [ ] **Agentic Integration**: Hook the client up to an LLM (e.g., via LangChain or standard OpenAI clients) so the LLM can *discover* the ODI tools and intelligently request customer insights when ideating features.

+# First-run wizard for The Living Studio — design
+
+**Status:** approved for implementation
+**Date:** 2026-10-21
+**Scope:** `apps/studio` (React SPA + Tauri shell). No sidecar, MCP, or API changes.
+
+## Intent
+
+A new user reaches The Living Studio and finds a chat box, a seed canvas, and a
+status-drenched header. The product can do four distinct things — map a job,
+score outcomes, simulate a bet, trace evidence — but nothing in the interface
+tells them that before they have to read a wall of prose or discover a tab.
+
+The first-run wizard answers one question in the first ten seconds: **what is
+this, and what should I do first?** It does it as a short, calm, skippable tour
+that ends in a real action, not a slideshow. It is the only place in the product
+where we explain ourselves; everything after that is learned by doing.
+
+## Goals
+
+1. Orient a first-time user in under a minute: the job-to-be-done premise, the
+   four things the studio does, the state of their instruments.
+2. End on a **first move**: the wizard sends a goal-specific prompt into the
+   copilot and reveals the canvas, so the tour produces work rather than memory.
+3. Be resumable, skippable, and replayable. Never trap a user, never nag.
+4. Arrive as an **isolated module** with a **feature flag**. `App.tsx` gains two
+   lines; no canvas, chat, or API code knows the wizard exists.
+5. Behave like a first-class dialog: focus trap, Escape to skip, focus returned
+   on close, reduced-motion support, mobile layout, no layout shift.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- **No backend onboarding state.** A local-first studio remembers locally. No
+  account, no telemetry, no network call.
+- **No LLM-authored tour content.** Deterministic copy, shipped with the build.
+- **No product tour with spotlight overlays.** Highlighting unlabeled buttons
+  makes a small product feel like enterprise software. The wizard is the
+  orientation; the canvas is the reveal.
+- **No second settings UI.** The readiness step reuses the same config values
+  and the same `saveSettings` path; it only surfaces the three fields a blocked
+  user actually needs.
+
+## The flow
+
+Four steps, one progress rail, never more than two actions on screen.
+
+| Step | Question | What it does |
+|---|---|---|
+| 1. Welcome | *What is this?* | The JTBD premise in one headline, plus the three moves the studio supports. |
+| 2. Starting point | *Where do I begin?* | Four goal cards (job, outcomes, bet, evidence). The choice sets the landing tab and the first prompt. |
+| 3. Instruments | *Will it work?* | Live status for the sidecar, MCP server, and model. If the model is down, the three config fields are inline with **Save & test**, not a dead end. |
+| 4. First move | *What happens next?* | Shows the exact prompt the copilot will receive. **Send it** completes the tour and starts the work; **Open the canvas** completes it and just navigates. |
+
+Skip is available on every step as a quiet text action. Skipping and finishing
+are both remembered. The tour is replayable from **Settings → Replay the welcome
+tour**.
+
+Progress is persisted after every transition, so a user who closes the app on
+step 3 resumes on step 3.
+
+## Architecture
+
+```
+apps/studio/src/
+├── features/
+│   ├── flags.ts            ← generic feature-flag resolution (env → storage → query)
+│   └── flags.test.ts
+├── onboarding/
+│   ├── content.ts          ← steps + goals, the only place copy lives
+│   ├── machine.ts          ← pure state transitions (no React, no DOM)
+│   ├── storage.ts          ← versioned localStorage read/write, defensive
+│   ├── context.ts          ← context + useOnboarding hook
+│   ├── OnboardingProvider.tsx  ← auto-open, persistence, replay
+│   ├── FirstRunWizard.tsx  ← the dialog (uses StudioContext for health + actions)
+│   ├── icons.tsx           ← four line icons
+│   └── onboarding.css      ← colocated styles, same tokens as theme.css
+└── App.tsx                 ← <OnboardingProvider><Shell/><FirstRunWizard/></…>
+```
+
+Three separations keep this from becoming spaghetti:
+
+- **Content is data.** `content.ts` exports typed steps and goals. Changing copy
+  or adding a goal is a data edit, not a JSX edit.
+- **State is pure.** `machine.ts` has no React import and no storage access, so
+  the flow is unit-tested as plain functions. Persistence sits behind
+  `storage.ts`; the provider only wires them together.
+- **The UI is one component.** It reads the studio context but writes through
+  existing, already-public actions (`sendMessage`, `setActiveTab`,
+  `saveSettings`, `checkConnections`). No new global state for the canvas.
+
+### Feature flag
+
+`firstRunWizard` defaults **on** so the MVP is visible, and is resolved in this
+order:
+
+1. URL: `?flags=firstRunWizard:off` (QA without a rebuild)
+2. `localStorage["studio.flags.firstRunWizard"]` (`on`/`off`)
+3. `VITE_STUDIO_FIRST_RUN_WIZARD` (`1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `on`/`off`)
+4. Default: on
+
+When the flag is off the provider still mounts but is inert: no dialog, no
+replay entry in Settings, no storage writes. The module adds no dead code at
+runtime.
+
+## Design language
+
+The wizard inherits the studio's dark, indigo-accented surface and adds only
+what a modal needs: a blurred backdrop, a soft top glow, 20px radius, and a
+single accent. One idea per screen, generous whitespace, sentence-case copy with
+no exclamation marks. Numbers (`1 / 4`) and a segmented hairline rail replace a
+decorative stepper.
+
+Motion is 220–320ms with an ease-out curve, and fully removed under
+`prefers-reduced-motion`. Under 640px the panel becomes full-height and goal
+cards stack.
+
+Accessibility: `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal`, labelled by the step heading,
+focus moved to the heading on every step, Tab trapped inside the panel, Escape
+skips, focus restored to the opener on close, status rows announced as text
+rather than color alone.
+
+## Trade-offs
+
+- **Auto-open vs. discovery.** Auto-opening is right for a first run and wrong
+  forever after; the flag plus the stored completion handles both. The Settings
+  replay covers "I closed it too fast."
+- **Completion bumps engagement.** Finishing at engagement level 0 raises the
+  shell to level 1, revealing the canvas. The wizard is the graduation from
+  chat-only to spatial.
+- **Versioned completion.** `ONBOARDING_VERSION` is stored with the state. A
+  future content revision can deliberately re-introduce the tour by bumping it;
+  we do not bump it for copy edits.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- With no stored onboarding state and the flag on, the dialog appears once.
+- All four steps are reachable without a mouse; Escape skips; focus stays inside.
+- Finishing step 4 sends the selected goal's prompt, sets the matching canvas
+  tab, records completion, and closes.
+- Replaying from Settings restarts at step 1 regardless of completion.
+- With the flag off, nothing renders and Settings shows no replay entry.
+- `npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck`, `run lint`, `test -- --run`, and
+  `run build` all pass.

Ships as a browser SPA and as a **Tauri 2 desktop app** (`apps/studio/src-tauri/`). | +| **`apps/studio/`** (React + TypeScript + Vite) | **The Living Studio** front end — a spatial, conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation with an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous copilot. --- apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/memory.py	
+++ apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/memory.py	
@@ -0,0 +1,342 @@
+"""Local, private memory for the Living Studio.
+
+The Studio remembers three things: the conversation, the durable observations it
+has made about the PM, and the opportunity thesis those observations build
+toward. Everything lives in a local SQLite file. Nothing is sent anywhere except
+the compact context block that is added to the model's system prompt.
+
+The store is deliberately boring: append-only turns, mutable observations, and
+no hidden writes. An observation is a proposal until the PM confirms it.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import sqlite3
+import threading
+import uuid
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+OBSERVATION_KINDS = (
+    "career",
+    "opportunity",
+    "business",
+    "stakeholder",
+    "constraint",
+    "evidence",
+    "preference",
+)
+OBSERVATION_STATUSES = ("suggested", "confirmed", "dismissed")
+
+
+def default_db_path() -> str:
+    """Resolve the Studio memory database, preferring an explicit override."""
+    configured = os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB")
+    if configured:
+        return configured
+    return str(Path.home() / ".agentic-odi" / "studio.db")
+
+
+def _now() -> str:
+    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
+
+
+def _json_dumps(value: Any) -> str:
+    return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
+
+
+def _json_loads(value: str | None, fallback: Any) -> Any:
+    if not value:
+        return fallback
+    try:
+        return json.loads(value)
+    except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
+        return fallback
+
+
+class StudioMemory:
+    """SQLite-backed conversation and observation memory."""
+
+    def __init__(self, db_path: str | None = None) -> None:
+        self.db_path = db_path or default_db_path()
+        if self.db_path != ":memory:":
+            Path(self.db_path).expanduser().parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        self._lock = threading.RLock()
+        self._conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path, check_same_thread=False)
+        self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
+        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
+        self._init_db()
+
+    def _init_db(self) -> None:
+        with self._conn:
+            self._conn.executescript(
+                """
+                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS conversations (
+                    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+                    started_at TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
+                );
+
+                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS turns (
+                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
+                    conversation_id TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    role TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    content TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+                    parts TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
+                    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
+                );
+
+                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS observations (
+                    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+                    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    text TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    data TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
+                    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'suggested',
+                    confidence REAL,
+                    source_turn INTEGER,
+                    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
+                );
+
+                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS turns_conversation
+                    ON turns(conversation_id, id);
+                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS observations_status
+                    ON observations(status, updated_at);
+                """
+            )
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------- conversations
+
+    def ensure_conversation(self, conversation_id: str | None = None) -> str:
+        conversation_id = conversation_id or str(uuid.uuid4())
+        now = _now()
+        with self._lock, self._conn:
+            row = self._conn.execute(
+                "SELECT id FROM conversations WHERE id = ?", (conversation_id,)
+            ).fetchone()
+            if row is None:
+                self._conn.execute(
+                    "INSERT INTO conversations (id, started_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
+                    (conversation_id, now, now),
+                )
+            else:
+                self._conn.execute(
+                    "UPDATE conversations SET updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?",
+                    (now, conversation_id),
+                )
+        return conversation_id
+
+    def create_conversation(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        conversation_id = self.ensure_conversation()
+        return {
+            "id": conversation_id,
+            "started_at": _now(),
+            "updated_at": _now(),
+            "turns": [],
+        }
+
+    def append_turn(
+        self,
+        conversation_id: str,
+        role: str,
+        content: str,
+        parts: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
+    ) -> int:
+        self.ensure_conversation(conversation_id)
+        now = _now()
+        with self._lock, self._conn:
+            cursor = self._conn.execute(
+                """
+                INSERT INTO turns (conversation_id, role, content, parts, created_at)
+                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
+                """,
+                (conversation_id, role, content, _json_dumps(parts or []), now),
+            )
+            self._conn.execute(
+                "UPDATE conversations SET updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?",
+                (now, conversation_id),
+            )
+        return int(cursor.lastrowid or 0)
+
+    def latest_conversation(self) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+        with self._lock:
+            conversation = self._conn.execute(
+                """
+                SELECT id, started_at, updated_at FROM conversations
+                ORDER BY updated_at DESC, started_at DESC LIMIT 1
+                """
+            ).fetchone()
+            if conversation is None:
+                return None
+            turns = self._conn.execute(
+                "SELECT id, role, content, parts, created_at FROM turns "
+                "WHERE conversation_id = ? ORDER BY id ASC",
+                (conversation["id"],),
+            ).fetchall()
+        return {
+            "id": conversation["id"],
+            "started_at": conversation["started_at"],
+            "updated_at": conversation["updated_at"],
+            "turns": [self._turn(row) for row in turns],
+        }
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _turn(row: sqlite3.Row) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "id": row["id"],
+            "role": row["role"],
+            "content": row["content"],
+            "parts": _json_loads(row["parts"], []),
+            "created_at": row["created_at"],
+        }
+
+    # -------------------------------------------------------------- observations
+
+    def add_observation(
+        self,
+        kind: str,
+        text: str,
+        data: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+        confidence: float | None = None,
+        source_turn: int | None = None,
+    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        if kind not in OBSERVATION_KINDS:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unknown observation kind: {kind}")
+        cleaned = text.strip()
+        if not cleaned:
+            raise ValueError("An observation needs some text")
+        if confidence is not None:
+            confidence = max(0.0, min(1.0, float(confidence)))
+
+        observation_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
+        now = _now()
+        with self._lock, self._conn:
+            self._conn.execute(
+                """
+                INSERT INTO observations
+                    (id, kind, text, data, status, confidence, source_turn, created_at, updated_at)
+                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'suggested', ?, ?, ?, ?)
+                """,
+                (
+                    observation_id,
+                    kind,
+                    cleaned,
+                    _json_dumps(data or {}),
+                    confidence,
+                    source_turn,
+                    now,
+                    now,
+                ),
+            )
+            row = self._conn.execute(
+                "SELECT * FROM observations WHERE id = ?", (observation_id,)
+            ).fetchone()
+        return self._observation(row)
+
+    def update_observation(
+        self,
+        observation_id: str,
+        status: str | None = None,
+        text: str | None = None,
+    ) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+        if status is not None and status not in OBSERVATION_STATUSES:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unknown observation status: {status}")
+        if text is not None and not text.strip():
+            raise ValueError("An observation needs some text")
+
+        updates: list[str] = []
+        values: list[Any] = []
+        if status is not None:
+            updates.append("status = ?")
+            values.append(status)
+        if text is not None:
+            updates.append("text = ?")
+            values.append(text.strip())
+        if not updates:
+            with self._lock:
+                row = self._conn.execute(
+                    "SELECT * FROM observations WHERE id = ?", (observation_id,)
+                ).fetchone()
+            return self._observation(row) if row else None
+
+        updates.append("updated_at = ?")
+        values.append(_now())
+        values.append(observation_id)
+        with self._lock, self._conn:
+            cursor = self._conn.execute(
+                f"UPDATE observations SET {', '.join(updates)} WHERE id = ?",
+                values,
+            )
+            if cursor.rowcount == 0:
+                return None
+            row = self._conn.execute(
+                "SELECT * FROM observations WHERE id = ?", (observation_id,)
+            ).fetchone()
+        return self._observation(row)
+
+    def list_observations(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+        with self._lock:
+            rows = self._conn.execute(
+                "SELECT * FROM observations ORDER BY updated_at DESC"
+            ).fetchall()
+        return [self._observation(row) for row in rows]
+
+    def context_block(self) -> str:
+        observations = self.list_observations()
+        confirmed = [item for item in observations if item["status"] == "confirmed"]
+        suggested = [item for item in observations if item["status"] == "suggested"]
+
+        if not confirmed and not suggested:
+            return (
+                "You do not know anything about this PM yet. Start with the opportunity "
+                "they want to chase, or the win they want to be known for."
+            )
+
+        lines = [
+            "What you already know about this PM. Use it. Do not re-ask it. If it is wrong, "
+            "invite a correction."
+        ]
+        if confirmed:
+            lines.append("Confirmed:")
+            lines.extend(f"- [{item['kind']}] {item['text']}" for item in confirmed[:24])
+        if suggested:
+            lines.append("Still checking (only mention if relevant):")
+            lines.extend(f"- [{item['kind']}] {item['text']}" for item in suggested[:12])
+        return "\n".join(lines)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _observation(row: sqlite3.Row) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "id": row["id"],
+            "kind": row["kind"],
+            "text": row["text"],
+            "data": _json_loads(row["data"], {}),
+            "status": row["status"],
+            "confidence": row["confidence"],
+            "source_turn": row["source_turn"],
+            "created_at": row["created_at"],
+            "updated_at": row["updated_at"],
+        }
+
+    # -------------------------------------------------------------------- house
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        with self._lock, self._conn:
+            self._conn.execute("DELETE FROM turns")
+            self._conn.execute("DELETE FROM conversations")
+            self._conn.execute("DELETE FROM observations")
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        with self._lock:
+            self._conn.close()
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "OBSERVATION_KINDS",
+    "OBSERVATION_STATUSES",
+    "StudioMemory",
+    "default_db_path",
+]

+

+    monkeypatch.setattr(chat, "check_llm_health", _healthy)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(chat, "McpClient", _Mcp)

+"""Tests for the memory and conversation endpoints."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import socket
+from typing import Any
+
+from agentic_odi_core import InMemoryRepository
+from agentic_odi_studio_api.app import create_app
+from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.memory import StudioMemory
+from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
+
+
+def _closed_url(path: str) -> str:
+    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as sock:
+        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        port = sock.getsockname()[1]
+    return f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}{path}"
+
+
+def _client(memory: StudioMemory | None = None) -> TestClient:
+    return TestClient(
+        create_app(InMemoryRepository(), memory=memory or StudioMemory(":memory:"))
+    )
+
+
+def _chat_body(conversation_id: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    return {
+        "base_url": _closed_url("/v1"),
+        "api_key": "k",
+        "model": "m",
+        "mcp_url": _closed_url("/mcp"),
+        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "I want to own activation."}],
+        "conversation_id": conversation_id,
+    }
+
+
+def test_memory_starts_empty() -> None:
+    response = _client().get("/api/memory")
+
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert response.json() == {"observations": []}
+
+
+def test_observation_can_be_created_confirmed_and_dismissed() -> None:
+    client = _client()
+
+    created = client.post(
+        "/api/memory/observations",
+        json={"kind": "career", "text": "Wants to be known for activation."},
+    )
+    assert created.status_code == 200
+    observation = created.json()["observation"]
+    assert observation["status"] == "suggested"
+
+    confirmed = client.patch(
+        f"/api/memory/observations/{observation['id']}", json={"status": "confirmed"}
+    )
+    assert confirmed.status_code == 200
+    assert confirmed.json()["observation"]["status"] == "confirmed"
+
+    dismissed = client.patch(
+        f"/api/memory/observations/{observation['id']}", json={"status": "dismissed"}
+    )
+    assert dismissed.status_code == 200
+    assert dismissed.json()["observation"]["status"] == "dismissed"
+
+
+def test_observation_not_found_returns_404() -> None:
+    response = _client().patch("/api/memory/observations/missing", json={"status": "confirmed"})
+
+    assert response.status_code == 404
+
+
+def test_invalid_observation_is_rejected() -> None:
+    response = _client().post(
+        "/api/memory/observations", json={"kind": "random", "text": "Nope"}
+    )
+
+    assert response.status_code == 422
+
+
+def test_delete_memory_clears_observations_and_conversations() -> None:
+    memory = StudioMemory(":memory:")
+    client = _client(memory)
+    client.post("/api/memory/observations", json={"kind": "career", "text": "Known for X."})
+    client.post("/api/conversations")
+
+    response = client.delete("/api/memory")
+
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert client.get("/api/memory").json() == {"observations": []}
+    assert client.get("/api/conversations/latest").json() == {"conversation": None}
+
+
+def test_latest_conversation_is_null_before_the_first_chat() -> None:
+    response = _client().get("/api/conversations/latest")
+
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert response.json() == {"conversation": None}
+
+
+def test_new_conversation_is_empty_and_latest() -> None:
+    client = _client()
+
+    created = client.post("/api/conversations")
+
+    assert created.status_code == 200
+    conversation = created.json()["conversation"]
+    assert conversation["turns"] == []
+    assert client.get("/api/conversations/latest").json()["conversation"]["id"] == conversation["id"]
+
+
+def test_chat_persists_the_exchange_against_the_conversation() -> None:
+    memory = StudioMemory(":memory:")
+    client = _client(memory)
+    conversation = client.post("/api/conversations").json()["conversation"]
+
+    with client.stream(
+        "POST", "/api/chat", json=_chat_body(conversation["id"])
+    ) as response:
+        assert response.status_code == 200
+        body = "".join(response.iter_text())
+
+    assert "event: conversation" in body
+    latest = client.get("/api/conversations/latest").json()["conversation"]
+    assert latest["id"] == conversation["id"]
+    assert [turn["role"] for turn in latest["turns"]] == ["user", "assistant"]
+    assert latest["turns"][0]["content"] == "I want to own activation."
+    assert latest["turns"][1]["parts"][0]["kind"] == "text"

 # Development
 
 Everything below mirrors what CI runs. Install the workspace first:
 
 ```bash
 uv sync --all-packages
 ```
 
 ## Linting, Formatting & Type Checks
 
 ```bash
 # Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml)
 uv run ruff check .
 uv run ruff format --check .
 
 # Type checking (run per project so each project's config applies)
 uv run --directory core mypy .
 uv run --directory mcp_server mypy .
 uv run --directory local_server mypy .
 uv run --directory client mypy .
 uv run --directory cli mypy .
 uv run --directory connectors mypy .
 uv run --directory website mypy .
 
 # Security scanning
 uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src website/
 ```
 
 ## Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio)
 
 The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally:
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix apps/studio run lint       # ESLint
 npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
 npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run  # Vitest (run once)
 npm --prefix apps/studio run build      # production build → apps/studio/dist
 cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
 ```
 
 ### Conversational UI coverage
 
 The agent-composed surfaces are covered at three levels:
 
 | File | What it covers |
 |---|---|

 ## Formatting workflow
 
 - **When editing Python files**, either rely on the **pre-commit hooks** below
   (recommended) or run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:
 
   ```bash
   uv run ruff format .
   ```
 
 - **CI behavior**:
   - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files.
   - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only.
   - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the
     changes, and push again.
 
 ## Pre-commit hooks
 
 To run the checks automatically before each commit:
 
 ```bash
 uv tool install pre-commit
 pre-commit install
 ```
 
 After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` run on staged files whenever you commit.
 You can also trigger them manually:
 
 ```bash
 pre-commit run --all-files
 ```
 
 ## Testing
 
 Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely
 in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests:
 
 ```bash
 uv run --directory core pytest
 uv run --directory mcp_server pytest
 uv run --directory local_server pytest
 uv run --directory client pytest
 uv run --directory cli pytest
 uv run --directory connectors pytest
 ```
 
 ## Test Coverage
 
 CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12**, combines each package's
 coverage into one `coverage.xml`, and uploads it to
 [Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) from the 3.12 job. Each
 matrix job also stores its combined report as a build artifact.
 
 The Codecov upload authenticates with the `CODECOV_TOKEN` repository secret and
 is non-blocking (`fail_ci_if_error: false`), so a Codecov outage or a fork PR
 without secrets cannot fail the test job. The badge at the top of the README
 tracks `main`, which is the baseline every PR is compared against:
 
 - **Project** status requires at least **90%** coverage (`target: 90%`) and
   tolerates a 1% dip from `codecov.yml`.
 - **Patch** status is informational for now, so new code can land while the
   suite catches up.
 
 To reproduce the combined report locally, run each package with its own coverage
 file and merge them the way CI does:
 
 ```bash
 set -e
 for pkg in core mcp_server local_server client cli connectors; do
   # Absolute path, so each package writes to the repo root rather than its own directory.
   COVERAGE_FILE="$PWD/.coverage.$pkg" uv run --directory "$pkg" pytest --cov="$pkg" -q
 done
 uv run coverage combine .coverage.*
 uv run coverage xml -o coverage.xml && uv run coverage report
 ```
 
 > [!NOTE]
 > Coverage is only collected for the Python packages. `studio/` and test
 > directories are excluded in `codecov.yml`.

   `test_*.py`.

 # Running The Living Studio
 
 **The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
 an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
 Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
 connected to the MCP server.
 
 The Studio runs three ways. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to
 the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM
 directly.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 ```text
 ┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
 │  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  local_server (sidecar)       │
 │  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
 │  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
 └────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                              │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                              └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                              │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                              ▼
                                              ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                              │  mcp_server  :8000/mcp        │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                              ▲
                                                              │ OpenAI-compatible
                                              ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                              │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
 ```
 
 ## 1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix studio run build   # build the SPA into studio/dist
 python -m client.run            # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100
 ```
 
 | Service | URL |
 |---|---|
 | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
 | Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 |
 
 `python -m client.run` starts both processes concurrently; press **Ctrl+C** to
 stop both.
 
 ## 2. Web — dev with hot reload
 
 Vite proxies `/api` to the sidecar:
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix studio run dev:full   # MCP + sidecar + Vite together
 # open http://localhost:5173
 ```
 
 ## 3. Desktop — Tauri 2
 
 The app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself:
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix studio run tauri dev     # dev window
 npm --prefix studio run tauri build   # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows)
 ```
 
 > [!NOTE]
 > **Tauri prerequisites.** The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and
 > Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu:
 >
 > ```bash
 > sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \
 >   libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64
 > ```
 >
 > The Tauri CLI ships as the `@tauri-apps/cli` npm dev dependency
 > (`npm --prefix studio run tauri`). The sidecar is launched with
 > `uv run python -m …` from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the
 > repo root, set `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT`.
 
 ## Desktop signing & updater secrets
 
 Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an
 unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub
 Actions secrets.
 
 | Secret | Purpose |
 |---|---|
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate`. |
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). |
 | `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. |
 | `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. |
 | `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. |
 | `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. |
 
 Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag
 is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via
 **Settings → Check for updates**.
 
 ### Managing the updater signing key
 
 The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can
 verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is
 embedded in `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is
 safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in
 CI, or attached to a build artifact.
 
 1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a
    passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:
 
    ```bash
    npm --prefix studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f
    ```
 
    This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub`
    (public).
 
 2. **Paste the public key** into `studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`:
 
    ```jsonc
    {
      "plugins": {
        "updater": {
          "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
          "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
 
 3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is
    git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:
 
    ```bash
    mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
    mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
    chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    ```
 
    Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/
    Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives.
    Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing
    installs.
 
 4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and
    variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:
 
    ```bash
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password
    ```
 
 5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed):
 
    ```bash
    gh secret list
    ```
 
 6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the
    new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into
    their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public
    key ahead of the cut-over.
 
 > [!CAUTION]
 > If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new
 > pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.
 
 > [!IMPORTANT]
 > **Migration note.** The Streamlit UI (`client/src/client/app.py`) has been
 > removed. The Living Studio now lives in `studio/` (browser SPA + Tauri desktop
 > app) and is served by the `local_server` sidecar on port **8100** (previously
 > Streamlit's `8501`). Start everything with `python -m client.run`. All
 > `AGENTIC_ODI_*` environment variable names, the demo dataset, and the ODI
 > formulas are unchanged.
 
 ## Rich responses
 
 The copilot does not only talk. When a surface carries the evidence better than a
 paragraph, the agent renders one **inline in the conversation**: a scored
 outcome, a ranked opportunity board, a before/after simulation of a bet, a
 customer quote with its lineage, the eight-stage job map, or a decision record.
 Three properties keep this safe and cheap to extend:
 
 - **The catalog is closed and owned by the SPA.**
   `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` declares nine primitives and six cards, their
   JSON Schema props, and the description the model reads. There is no HTML, no
   eval, and no third-party component in the path.
 - **The sidecar is catalog-agnostic.** The SPA sends the catalog with each turn;
   the sidecar derives the `render_ui` tool schema from it, validates what comes
   back, and streams a `ui` SSE event. Invalid props return to the model as a tool
   result naming the exact violation, so a fumbled prop is corrected in the same
   reply. A client that sends no catalog never sees the tool.
 - **Cards are views, never actors.** Every button is an `intent` string that the
   agent receives as the user's next message — one authority, one audit trail.
 
 A surface is one node tree, streamed as one event:
 
 ```json
 {
   "type": "outcome-card",
   "props": {
     "id": "O-1",
     "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments",
     "importance": 9,
     "satisfaction": 3
   }
 }
 ```
 
 The opportunity score is computed from importance and satisfaction when the
 agent omits it, so the ODI formula has exactly one home (`src/lib/odi.ts`).
 Unknown component types degrade to a quiet fallback; a tree that fails
 validation is dropped whole, and the surrounding prose still reads.
 
 Run the sidecar without a model and the demo still renders real cards — that
-path is what a first-run user sees, and it exercises every card type in CI.
+path is what a first-run user reaches after the tour, and it exercises every
+card type in CI.
 
 ### Adding a surface
 
 1. Add an entry to `CATALOG` in `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` — props as a
    JSON Schema subset, plus the description the model will read.
 2. Register the component in `apps/studio/src/ui/registry.ts`.
 3. Implement it in `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx` (domain shape) or
    `apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx` (composition).
 4. Run `npm --prefix apps/studio test`. The `registry parity` test fails if the
    catalog and the registry drift apart.
 
 No server change is needed, and no new dependency.
 
+## First-run wizard
+
+A new user is greeted by a four-step tour before the canvas: what the studio is,
+which of the four starting points they want, the live state of their sidecar /
+MCP server / model (with inline repair when the model is down), and the exact
+first prompt the copilot will receive. The last step sends that prompt and
+reveals the canvas at the matching tab, so the tour ends in real work.
+
+The tour is skippable (footer action or `Escape`) and resumable: progress is
+stored after every step in `localStorage["studio.onboarding"]`. Replay it any
+time from **Settings → Replay the welcome tour** — the header's settings control
+makes that reachable from the first-run shell.
+
+Everything lives in `apps/studio/src/onboarding/`:
+
+| File | Role |
+|---|---|
+| `content.ts` | Steps and goal copy as typed data — the only place the words live |
+| `machine.ts` | Pure state transitions, no React or storage |
+| `storage.ts` | Versioned, defensive `localStorage` persistence |
+| `OnboardingProvider.tsx` | Auto-open, persistence, replay |
+| `FirstRunWizard.tsx`, `steps.tsx`, `onboarding.css` | The dialog |
+| `../features/flags.ts` | The `firstRunWizard` toggle |
+
+The app only wires the provider and the wizard into `App.tsx`; the canvas, chat,
+and API code are untouched.
+
+### Toggling the wizard
+
+`firstRunWizard` defaults to on. Resolution order, highest first:
+
+| Source | Example | Use |
+|---|---|---|
+| Query parameter | `?flags=firstRunWizard:off` | QA a build without rebuilding |
+| Local override | `localStorage["studio.flags.firstRunWizard"] = "off"` | Per-browser opt-out |
+| Build environment | `VITE_STUDIO_FIRST_RUN_WIZARD=off npm --prefix apps/studio run build` | Ship it dark |
+| Default | on | |
+
+Accepted values are `1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `on`/`off`, `yes`/`no`, and
+`enabled`/`disabled`. With the flag off, no dialog renders, no onboarding state
+is written, and Settings hides the replay action.
+
 ## Connecting an LLM
 
 The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM backend with tool-calling support to
 drive the agent. For a fully local setup, see
 [Local LLM Backend](local-llm.md).
 
 ## Agent-Driven Testing
 
 Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it starts
 both processes, opens the browser, sends a test message, and reports the results.
 
 Type `/test` to have the agent run all tests and report the results
 automatically.

+# Intent-First PM Experience Implementation Plan
+
+> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
+
+**Goal:** Make the Living Studio open with the PM's next career-defining opportunity, translate it into ODI underneath, remember it locally, and show what it learned.
+
+**Architecture:** A new local `StudioMemory` SQLite store owns conversations, turns, and observations. The sidecar injects a compact memory block into the system prompt, exposes a `remember` tool, and persists every turn. The React client resumes the latest conversation, renders a new Opportunity Thesis card, and ships a **What I've learned** panel. Copy and onboarding move from framework-first to ambition-first.
+
+**Tech Stack:** Python 3.10+, FastAPI, FastMCP, SQLite, pytest; React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Vitest.
+
+**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-intent-first-pm-experience-design.md`
+
+## Global Constraints
+
+- Local-first; no new network calls, no transcript/secret logging.
+- `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB` overrides the memory database path; tests use `:memory:`.
+- Keep the existing MCP domain and ODI scoring intact.
+- No emojis in product chrome.
+- Copy is warm, direct, encouraging, humble, and thankful.
+- Update README/docs in the same task.
+
+## Review Focus
+
+1. A first-time PM can begin without typing an ODI term.
+2. A resumed session restores both prose and agent-composed cards.
+3. `remember` never blocks the reply and never writes silently on the PM's behalf.
+4. A failed memory read/write degrades to the conversation working, not a broken screen.
+5. Demo evidence is never presented as the PM's real evidence.
+
+---
+
+### Task 1: Studio memory store
+
+**Files:**
+- Create: `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/memory.py`
+- Test: `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_memory.py`
+
+**Interfaces:**
+- `StudioMemory(db_path: str | None = None)`
+- `ensure_conversation(conversation_id: str | None = None) -> str`
+- `append_turn(conversation_id: str, role: str, content: str, parts: list[dict] | None = None) -> int`
+- `latest_conversation() -> dict | None`
+- `create_conversation() -> dict`
+- `add_observation(kind, text, data=None, confidence=None, source_turn=None) -> dict`
+- `update_observation(observation_id, status=None, text=None) -> dict | None`
+- `list_observations() -> list[dict]`
+- `context_block() -> str`
+- `clear() -> None`
+
+- [ ] Write tests for round-tripping turns and parts, observation lifecycle, context block, and clearing.
+- [ ] Implement the SQLite store with WAL, `:memory:` support, and JSON columns.
+- [ ] Run `uv run --directory apps/studio-api pytest tests/test_studio_memory.py -q`.
+
+### Task 2: Agent prompt, `remember`, and turn persistence
+
+**Files:**
+- Modify: `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py`

 # First-run wizard for The Living Studio — design
 
 **Status:** approved for implementation
 **Date:** 2026-10-21
 **Scope:** `apps/studio` (React SPA + Tauri shell). No sidecar, MCP, or API changes.
 
 ## Intent
 
 A new user reaches The Living Studio and finds a chat box, a seed canvas, and a
 status-drenched header. The product can do four distinct things — map a job,
 score outcomes, simulate a bet, trace evidence — but nothing in the interface
 tells them that before they have to read a wall of prose or discover a tab.
 
 The first-run wizard answers one question in the first ten seconds: **what is
 this, and what should I do first?** It does it as a short, calm, skippable tour
 that ends in a real action, not a slideshow. It is the only place in the product
 where we explain ourselves; everything after that is learned by doing.
 
 ## Goals
 
 1. Orient a first-time user in under a minute: the job-to-be-done premise, the
    four things the studio does, the state of their instruments.
 2. End on a **first move**: the wizard sends a goal-specific prompt into the
    copilot and reveals the canvas, so the tour produces work rather than memory.
 3. Be resumable, skippable, and replayable. Never trap a user, never nag.
 4. Arrive as an **isolated module** with a **feature flag**. `App.tsx` gains two
    lines; no canvas, chat, or API code knows the wizard exists.
 5. Behave like a first-class dialog: focus trap, Escape to skip, focus returned
    on close, reduced-motion support, mobile layout, no layout shift.
 
 ## Non-goals
 
 - **No backend onboarding state.** A local-first studio remembers locally. No
   account, no telemetry, no network call.
 - **No LLM-authored tour content.** Deterministic copy, shipped with the build.
 - **No product tour with spotlight overlays.** Highlighting unlabeled buttons
   makes a small product feel like enterprise software. The wizard is the
   orientation; the canvas is the reveal.
 - **No second settings UI.** The readiness step reuses the same config values
   and the same `saveSettings` path; it only surfaces the three fields a blocked
   user actually needs.
 
 ## The flow
 
 Four steps, one progress rail, never more than two actions on screen.
 
 | Step | Question | What it does |
 |---|---|---|
 | 1. Welcome | *What is this?* | The JTBD premise in one headline, plus the three moves the studio supports. |
 | 2. Starting point | *Where do I begin?* | Four goal cards (job, outcomes, bet, evidence). The choice sets the landing tab and the first prompt. |
 | 3. Instruments | *Will it work?* | Live status for the sidecar, MCP server, and model. If the model is down, the three config fields are inline with **Save & test**, not a dead end. |
 | 4. First move | *What happens next?* | Shows the exact prompt the copilot will receive. **Send it** completes the tour and starts the work; **Open the canvas** completes it and just navigates. |
 
-Skip is available on every step as a quiet text action. Skipping and finishing
-are both remembered. The tour is replayable from **Settings → Replay the welcome
-tour**.
+Skip is a quiet text action on steps 1–3, and `Escape` exits from any step
+(including the last). Skipping and finishing are both remembered, and both
+reveal the canvas. The tour is replayable from **Settings → Replay the welcome
+tour**; the new header control makes Settings reachable from the first-run
+shell.
 
 Progress is persisted after every transition, so a user who closes the app on
 step 3 resumes on step 3.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 ```
 apps/studio/src/
 ├── features/
 │   ├── flags.ts            ← generic feature-flag resolution (env → storage → query)
 │   └── flags.test.ts
 ├── onboarding/
 │   ├── content.ts          ← steps + goals, the only place copy lives
 │   ├── machine.ts          ← pure state transitions (no React, no DOM)
 │   ├── storage.ts          ← versioned localStorage read/write, defensive
 │   ├── context.ts          ← context + useOnboarding hook
 │   ├── OnboardingProvider.tsx  ← auto-open, persistence, replay
 │   ├── FirstRunWizard.tsx  ← the dialog (uses StudioContext for health + actions)
 │   ├── icons.tsx           ← four line icons
 │   └── onboarding.css      ← colocated styles, same tokens as theme.css
 └── App.tsx                 ← <OnboardingProvider><Shell/><FirstRunWizard/></…>
 ```
 
 Three separations keep this from becoming spaghetti:
 
 - **Content is data.** `content.ts` exports typed steps and goals. Changing copy
   or adding a goal is a data edit, not a JSX edit.
 - **State is pure.** `machine.ts` has no React import and no storage access, so
   the flow is unit-tested as plain functions. Persistence sits behind
   `storage.ts`; the provider only wires them together.
 - **The UI is one component.** It reads the studio context but writes through
   existing, already-public actions (`sendMessage`, `setActiveTab`,
   `saveSettings`, `checkConnections`). No new global state for the canvas.
 
 ### Feature flag
 
 `firstRunWizard` defaults **on** so the MVP is visible, and is resolved in this
 order:
 
 1. URL: `?flags=firstRunWizard:off` (QA without a rebuild)
 2. `localStorage["studio.flags.firstRunWizard"]` (`on`/`off`)
 3. `VITE_STUDIO_FIRST_RUN_WIZARD` (`1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `on`/`off`)
 4. Default: on
 
 When the flag is off the provider still mounts but is inert: no dialog, no
 replay entry in Settings, no storage writes. The module adds no dead code at
 runtime.
 
 ## Design language
 
 The wizard inherits the studio's dark, indigo-accented surface and adds only
 what a modal needs: a blurred backdrop, a soft top glow, 20px radius, and a
 single accent. One idea per screen, generous whitespace, sentence-case copy with
 no exclamation marks. Numbers (`1 / 4`) and a segmented hairline rail replace a
 decorative stepper.
 
 Motion is 220–320ms with an ease-out curve, and fully removed under
 `prefers-reduced-motion`. Under 640px the panel becomes full-height and goal
 cards stack.
 
 Accessibility: `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal`, labelled by the step heading,
 focus moved to the heading on every step, Tab trapped inside the panel, Escape
 skips, focus restored to the opener on close, status rows announced as text
 rather than color alone.
 
 ## Trade-offs
 
 - **Auto-open vs. discovery.** Auto-opening is right for a first run and wrong
   forever after; the flag plus the stored completion handles both. The Settings
   replay covers "I closed it too fast."
-- **Completion bumps engagement.** Finishing at engagement level 0 raises the
-  shell to level 1, revealing the canvas. The wizard is the graduation from
-  chat-only to spatial.
+- **Completion bumps engagement.** Finishing or skipping at engagement level 0
+  raises the shell to level 1, revealing the canvas. The wizard is the
+  graduation from chat-only to spatial, not a gate.
 - **Versioned completion.** `ONBOARDING_VERSION` is stored with the state. A
   future content revision can deliberately re-introduce the tour by bumping it;
   we do not bump it for copy edits.
 
 ## Acceptance criteria
 
 - With no stored onboarding state and the flag on, the dialog appears once.
 - All four steps are reachable without a mouse; Escape skips; focus stays inside.
 - Finishing step 4 sends the selected goal's prompt, sets the matching canvas
   tab, records completion, and closes.
 - Replaying from Settings restarts at step 1 regardless of completion.
 - With the flag off, nothing renders and Settings shows no replay entry.
 - `npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck`, `run lint`, `test -- --run`, and
   `run build` all pass.

+# Intent-First PM Experience Design
+
+**Date:** 2026-10-21
+**Status:** Approved for implementation
+**Scope:** The Living Studio's first-run flow, conversation, memory, default canvas, and supporting sidecar API.
+
+## Intent & Why
+
+Product managers are judged on the opportunities they choose and the outcomes they deliver. They arrive with an ambition, a mandate, or a vague itch — not with a request for a methodology. The current Studio opens with Outcome-Driven Innovation vocabulary and treats the framework as the destination. That is backwards.
+
+The Studio should be the PM's strategist: it listens for the opportunity they want to chase, translates their intent into rigorous structures underneath, remembers what it learns, and shows its work. ODI remains the engine. It is never the greeting.
+
+**North star:** *Help me choose and win the next opportunity that matters — to my customers, my business, and my career.*
+
+Understanding the business and deciding what to build are stepping stones to that. They are evidence for the opportunity thesis, not the opening question.
+
+## Goals
+
+- Open the first conversation with the PM's ambition, not the framework.
+- Make the Opportunity Thesis the central artifact of the product.
+- Remember the PM: transcript, durable observations, and the thesis, stored locally.
+- Show what the agent learned, as it learns it, with accept/edit/dismiss.
+- Remove ODI terminology from default surfaces; keep a deliberate expert view.
+- Use warm, direct, encouraging, humble, and thankful copy.
+- Isolate demo data so it can never masquerade as the PM's evidence.
+
+## Non-Goals
+
+- Multi-user accounts, cloud sync, or team collaboration.
+- A full stakeholder-map or business-case builder in this slice.
+- Replacing the MCP domain model or the ODI scoring implementation.
+- A complete visual redesign. We reuse the existing design language.
+- Automatic LLM extraction independent of the agent's `remember` tool.
+
+## Experience
+
+### First run
+
+One screen, one question:
+
+> **What would make this a year to remember?**
+> The opportunity you'd be proud to own. Not a backlog. Not a roadmap.
+
+Four doors:
+
+- I have an opportunity in mind.
+- My boss handed me a priority.
+- I need to find one.
+- Pressure-test an idea.
+
+Connection readiness is a quiet second step: "Let's make sure I can hear you." Technical configuration is collapsed under **Advanced**. The first prompt is written as the PM would speak, not as an ODI request.
+
+### Conversation
+
+The agent asks one question at a time. It starts with the opportunity or the win, then learns about the PM, then the customer, the business, and the people who need to say yes. It reflects back before advising:
+
+> Here's the opportunity I hear… The outcome… The business case… The career case… What I'm still unsure about… Does that sound like your world?
+
+If the PM does not know what to chase, the agent runs a discovery path: what is changing, where the workaround is ugly, what they could uniquely own. It offers three hypotheses, each with why now and why them. Familiar examples and market-gap archetypes are inspiration, never a lecture.
+
+### Canvas
+
+The default view is **Your next move**: the thesis and the opportunities in play. Supporting views:
+
+- **What I've learned** — the memory, editable.
+- **The evidence** — customer signals, business data, market context.
+- **How the work happens** — the job map, in plain language.
+- **What changes if we do this** — the bet simulation.
+- **Add what you know** — manual capture, in plain language.
+- **Show the ODI view** — the expert layer: outcomes, scores, formula, job stages.
+
+### Returning
+
+The Studio resumes the latest conversation and memory. The PM can let the structure sit, or open **What I've learned** and edit it. Memory can be exported or deleted from Settings.
+
+## Data
+
+Local SQLite database at `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB` or `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db`.
+
+### Conversations and turns
+
+- `conversations(id, started_at, updated_at)`
+- `turns(id, conversation_id, role, content, parts, created_at)`
+
+`parts` is JSON: text and agent-composed UI specs, in order. This lets a resumed transcript render exactly as it did live.
+
+### Observations
+
+- `observations(id, kind, text, data, status, confidence, source_turn, created_at, updated_at)`
+
+`kind`: `career`, `opportunity`, `business`, `stakeholder`, `constraint`, `evidence`, `preference`.
+
+`status`: `suggested`, `confirmed`, `dismissed`. The agent proposes; the PM confirms. Confirmed and suggested observations both inform the agent, clearly labelled.
+
+### Opportunity thesis
+
+The thesis is stored as an observation of kind `opportunity` with structured `data`, and rendered as a dedicated card. Fields:
+
+- title, opportunity, outcome
+- business value, career value, right to win
+- beliefs, evidence have, evidence need
+- stakeholders, next proof
+- confidence, status (`exploring`, `validating`, `committed`, `parked`)
+
+## API
+
+- `GET /api/memory` → `{ observations: Observation[] }`
+- `POST /api/memory/observations` → create one
+- `PATCH /api/memory/observations/{id}` → confirm, dismiss, or edit
+- `DELETE /api/memory` → clear all memory
+- `GET /api/conversations/latest` → latest conversation with turns
+- `POST /api/conversations` → start a fresh conversation
+- `POST /api/chat` accepts an optional `conversation_id`; the sidecar persists the user turn and the final assistant turn.
+
+## Agent Behavior
+
+The system prompt is a translator's playbook, not an ODI syllabus.
+
+- Role: the PM's strategist and advocate. Warm, direct, honest. Never a framework tutor.
+- Start with ambition. Ask one question at a time. Reflect before advising.
+- Translate to ODI silently. Use "job", "outcome", or "opportunity score" only if the PM does.
+- Call `remember` when a durable fact is learned. Never narrate the mechanics of remembering.
+- Use `render_ui` for the Opportunity Thesis card once there is enough to show. One surface, one short sentence.
+- Label assumptions. Never invent evidence or customer quotes.
+- Challenge with care: "Is this a real opportunity, or a visible project?" "Will this still matter in two years?"
+- Tone: encouraging, humble, thankful. No flattery, therapy-speak, emojis, or corporate jargon.
+
+## Copy Rules
+
+- Say the human thing. "What are you trying to make happen?" not "Define the job."
+- Keep the promise generous: *Your next signature move.*
+- Name the career stake without cynicism: scope, visibility, skills, relationships, optionality.
+- Advanced terminology is available, never required.
+- Every empty state teaches the next move.
+
+## Constraints
+
+- Local-first. No new network calls.
+- Do not log API keys, transcripts, or memory payloads.
+- Tests stay fast and isolated; the Studio memory store must use an in-memory database in tests.
+- Keep the existing MCP/ODI domain intact.
+- Update README and docs in the same task.
+
+## Success Signals
+
+- A PM reaches a confirmed opportunity thesis in under three minutes.
+- No ODI terms appear in the first session unless the PM uses them.
+- The PM confirms or edits the agent's observations.
+- Returning users resume with context.
+- Every agent-written memory item is visible and reversible.
+
+## Resolved Decisions
+

--- docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-living-studio-ux-design.md

@@ -0,0 +1,97 @@
+# Living Studio First-Impression & Readability UX Design
+
+**Date:** 2026-10-21
+**Status:** Approved for implementation
+**Scope:** The Living Studio's header, first impression / first-run shell, conversation framing, status surfaces, and copy.
+
+## Intent & Why
+
+The first moment a user reaches the Studio must point unambiguously at the one
+thing that matters: the conversation. Today the opening screen carries the
+product name in several places at once, surfaces a verbose status bar that
+churns, opens a settings panel full of inputs by default, and offers five
+near-duplicate starting buttons. The result is hard to read and unclear to
+focus.
+
+This change strips that noise so the eye has exactly one place to land — the
+chat — and every label says what it means the first time, once.
+
+**North star:** *Say the name once. Frame the conversation. Give one first move.*
+
+## Goals
+
+- The product name ("The Living Studio") appears exactly once on screen at any
+  moment, in the header.
+- No decorative subtitle or version pill competes with the header.
+- A single consolidated status pill replaces the three current status pills.
+- The welcome message does not restate the product name.
+- The conversation lives in a clear bordered frame; the canvas is secondary.
+- The first impression offers the fewest honest starting moves (two starter
+  pills + the input), with no duplicated buttons.
+- The settings drawer opens collapsed; its heading drops the redundant name.
+- Status text is quiet: a single stable line for canvas sync, and a single
+  "Working…" label for the thinking phase (motion stays as the dot pulse only).
+- The first-run wizard keeps its four honest goal choices and focus trap, but
+  its copy drops the product-name echo and tightens its lead line.
+
+## Non-Goals
+
+- A full visual redesign. Reuse the existing dark design language.
+- Changing the ODI domain model, scoring, or MCP tool surface.
+- Changing the canvas tab set or the canvas data model.
+- Adding new features, surfaces, or capabilities.
+
+## Experience
+
+### The shell, post-wizard (engagement 0 → 1 → 2)
+
+**Before.** Header reads "The Living Studio | Outcome-Driven Innovation"
+plus subtitle "A Canvas of Human Intent. Zero file trees. Real-time causality."
+plus three pills ("ODI Framework v1.0", LLM state, MCP state). Below it the
+chat head reads "Copilot / Speak your intent…", then the welcome message
+"Welcome to The Living Studio…". The settings drawer opens by default with
+four inputs and an "About the Living Studio" section. The canvas sync bar
+cycles emoji-laden text and a "source / cached · updating…" badge.
+
+**After.** Header reads just "The Living Studio" and one status pill
+("Live" / "Demo mode"). No subtitle. The chat is wrapped in a bordered
+`.chat-frame` so it is the clear stage. The welcome message is a single
+concise sentence with no name restatement. Starter pills reduced to
+"Define a job" and "Score the outcomes". The welcome card becomes pure
+intro text (its two action buttons are removed — they duplicated the pills).
+The settings drawer starts collapsed with heading "Controls". The sync bar
+is one stable line ("Canvas synced" / "Updating…"). The thinking phase is
+one stable label ("Working…") backed by the existing pulse.
+
+### The first-run wizard
+
+**Before.** Step 1 wordmark says "The Living Studio"; the step-1 lead then
+says "The Living Studio helps you…" — a name echo. The lead is 24 words.
+
+**After.** Wordmark stays (it is the only name shown during the tour). The
+lead drops the name and is tightened to one concise sentence. The four goal
+cards and the three-moves list are kept — they are the product's first
+decision, not clutter. The wizard's accessibility behavior (focus trap,
+Escape to skip, Tab containment) is unchanged.
+
+## Constraints
+
+- Keep all existing vitest tests green. Where copy changes break an assertion,
+  update the assertion to the new copy — but never weaken a behavioral test.
+- No emojis in product chrome: remove emojis from the status pills, the sync
+  bar, and any new status text. (Aligns with the project's existing
+  "No emojis in product chrome" convention.)
+- Local-first: no new network calls, no new runtime dependencies.
+- Update `docs/living-studio.md` in the same task if user-facing copy or
+  behavior changes that it describes.
+
+## Acceptance
+
+- Header renders exactly one visible occurrence of "Living Studio".
+- Settings drawer starts collapsed.
+- Sync bar renders a single line and never shows the cycling emoji text.
+- Thinking phase renders a single stable label.
+- Quick pills are exactly "Define a job" and "Score the outcomes".
+- Welcome card renders no action buttons.
+- Wizard step-1 lead does not contain "The Living Studio".
+- `npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck`, `lint`, and `test` all pass.

        run: |

Also any `.vitest-cache`. Use `git rm -r --cached node_modules` then leave files on disk. But if they are untracked and ignored, status clean. Do that.
